focal_region.annotated_sentence_text:
[Turn 1 USER]
e001	My friend Jonah and I have spent eighteen months making an audio documentary.
e002	We were invited to premiere it at a respected local showcase in six weeks.
e003	I produced the reporting and interviews; he built the sound and structure.
e004	After listening to the latest cut, I think the final third needs a major re-edit.
e005	Jonah thinks we should finish what we have and learn from an audience.
e006	We are also avoiding a conversation about whether the credit should simply say “by both of us” or name our roles.
[Turn 1 ASSISTANT]
e007	The edit and credit issues are related because both ask how your different contributions translate into authority.
e008	Six weeks may be enough for targeted revision but not for rebuilding the final third without sacrificing the rest.
e009	Before deciding, identify what problem you hear: factual confusion, emotional shape, pacing, or discomfort that the piece is becoming final.
e010	On credit, naming roles can recognize distinct work, but it should not become a substitute for agreeing who decides what.
[Turn 7 USER]
e063	My provisional plan is to hear Jonah's revised cut before deciding about postponement.
e064	I will compare it with the approved version and write down the exact interpretive difference I still see, if any.
e065	For credit, I will propose equal top-line authorship with detailed role credits below, but I am not sure I can accept that if he still treats structural decisions as his domain.
e066	I want to separate the current film from the rules for our next collaboration, and I am not sure they can really be separated.
[Turn 7 ASSISTANT]
e067	Listening before deciding prevents an abstract disagreement from hardening around a cut that does not yet exist.
e068	Your uncertainty about credit and future authority is also legitimate: a current credit can acknowledge completed work, while the feelings behind it may still determine whether you collaborate again.
e069	You do not need to solve the next project before the showcase, but you may need to avoid using a harmonious credit line as evidence that the underlying process felt mutual.
e070	The revised cut could resolve the edit question and leave the partnership question open.
